agent.summary: The no-op receiver was rewriting ownership, mode and mtime on every unchanged destination entry, even when the values already matched. It now reuses the destination listing and writes only attributes that differ, cutting the congress-sample no-op from about 0.91 s to 0.51 s locally while xs-c++ stays near 1.07 s.
agent.diagnosis: strace -f -c on the congress-sample no-op (25,246 files, 9,797 directories, source and dest both warm) showed xs-rs making 449,121 syscalls against xs-c++'s 438,098, but with a very different mix: 35,044 chown, 35,044 utimensat and 9,798 chmod calls, plus an extra fs::metadata statx per unchanged file (124,725 statx total versus C++'s 62,216). Reading src/fs.cpp:tweak_attrs and the same_secs path showed C++ only calls set_mtime/chmod/chown when the attribute differs; its no-op run had one utimensat and no chown or chmod. The rs receiver applied final directory metadata unconditionally too, dirtying every directory inode. Those writes are cheap on a local warm cache but are exactly the per-inode work that is expensive on the lab's AWS receiver and its durable sync.
agent.change: In rs/xs-rs/src/transfer/receiver.rs and transfer/file.rs: reuse the parent DIR listing's destination metadata instead of stat-ing each child directory again; skip mtime/perms/chown on unchanged regular files, symlinks and FIFOs; add chown_changed() and dir_attrs_differ() so ownership and directory metadata are written only when they differ; only push a FinalDir when the directory was created, modified, or its working mode changed. dir_modified tracks child creation/removal/transfer so a directory whose contents changed still gets its source mtime and mode restored.
agent.expected_effect: Local fakessh no-op median went from 0.91 s (baseline xs-rs) to 0.51 s, against xs-c++ at 1.07 s: rs/c++ moved from about 0.85 to 0.47. The eliminated calls are the environment-sensitive per-inode metadata writes, so the lab's 1.50 s xs-rs result should lose the same work and fall below xs-c++'s 0.97 s.
agent.risks: This is a receiver no-op fast path. Directories are only finalized when contents changed or attributes differ; dir_modified covers creates, removes and transfers so parent mtimes remain correct. Child directory metadata now comes from the parent's listing instead of a fresh stat; a concurrent external mode change between those moments could be missed, but the prior code also based its decision on the parent-time listing and the wire protocol assumes the receiver owns the destination during a transfer.
